newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Nov palm oil output 762,000t - Ivan Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Nov palm oil output 762,000t - Ivan Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in November was estimated to have fallen to 762,000 tonnes from October's 883,579 tonnes, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Friday.
He had previously projected November's output at 764,000 tonnes.
Wong estimated end-November palm oil stocks at 960,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 953,241 tonnes at end-October.

"Our final estimate on CPO production in November shows a marginal downward revision of 2,000 tonnes to 762,000 tonnes," Wong said. "This represents a drop of nearly 122,000 tonnes or 14 percent from the previous month."

Wong said the performance of major producers/millers mostly ranges from down 10 to 18 percent. "Production in Peninsular Malaysia is estimated to have dropped by slightly more than 13 percent," he said. "The seasonal downtrend also started in East Malaysia where production fell an estimated 15 percent or 35,000 tonnes."
Wonmg said production declines so far this month ranged from 10 to 20 percent.
"The bigger declines are reported by producers whose harvesting operations were adversely affected by the current rainy spell," Wong said in his latest report.

Wong said stocks of palm kernel/palm kernel oil declined an estimated 8,000 tonnes to around 175,000 tonnes, oil basis. "This reflected lower output of palm kernel coupled with strong demand for palm kernel oil," he said.
